title: Navigating the Digital World as Humans Do: Universal Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
research_question: Can a GUI agent relying only on screenshots and pixel-level actions achieve robust cross-platform operation when a specialized model grounds diverse referring expressions directly to interface coordinates?
methodology: The authors synthesize training triplets consisting of a GUI screenshot, a referring expression, and the target element coordinates, with the expected output defined as the element center point. They build UGround from a slightly adapted LLaVA-style visual grounding architecture and integrate it into the vision-only SeeAct-V agent framework, where an external multimodal planner produces textual plans and UGround maps those plans to screen coordinates. The approach is evaluated on grounding, offline-agent, and online-agent benchmarks spanning web, desktop, and mobile environments, with additional data-scale and referring-expression ablations.

key_findings.finding: On ScreenSpot in the standard grounding setting, the original UGround achieved 73.3 average accuracy versus 53.4 for SeeClick.
With GPT-4o-generated referring expressions in the ScreenSpot agent setting, UGround achieved 81.4 average grounding accuracy versus 52.3 for SeeClick.
Web-derived synthetic grounding data generalized across platforms, including desktop interfaces that were absent from the original UGround training data.
With only 50,000 training screenshots, representing about 600,000 elements, UGround already exceeded SeeClick by more than 10 percentage points in the reported scaling study.
Including positional referring expressions improved ScreenSpot grounding relative to removing positional referring expressions, especially in the standard setting.
key_findings.section: Appendix C.3, Tables C.3 and C.4

key_findings.finding: SeeAct-V agents using UGround were competitive with or better than prior agents on multiple offline and online benchmarks despite using screenshots rather than HTML or accessibility-tree observations for grounding.

limitations: The training corpus is extremely large and contains repeated or similar web elements, leaving substantial room for better data efficiency and deduplication.
Long-tail mobile and desktop interface elements remain under-addressed.
The original training mixture contains no desktop UI screenshots, which the authors identify as a limitation on desktop performance.
UGround requires an external planner and is not a standalone GUI agent.

The evaluated grounding target is a coordinate on a current GUI screenshot; the study does not evaluate cross-version document-element lineage, version identity, or hierarchical page-region-cell provenance.
raw_claims: UGround maps textual referring expressions for GUI elements directly to pixel coordinates.
The training data contains about 10 million GUI elements and referring expressions over about 1.3 million screenshots.
The synthetic grounding examples are generated primarily from webpages.
SeeAct-V separates planning from visual grounding and uses screenshots as its environmental observation.
UGround reached 73.3 average accuracy on the original ScreenSpot standard evaluation.
UGround reached 81.4 average accuracy with GPT-4o planner-generated referring expressions on ScreenSpot.
Training on web screenshots produced substantial transfer to mobile and desktop interfaces.
The data-scaling experiment showed strong results even with 50,000 training screenshots.
Positional referring expressions provide measurable grounding benefit.
The authors identify repetitive training data, long-tail elements, missing desktop training data, and dependence on an external planner as limitations.
